title: Remote inspector calls getters and setters when the running project is paused
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible: v4.8.dev.custom_build [457470a8d]

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev (457470a8d) - EndeavourOS #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue, 28 Jul 2026 13:49:51 +0000 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 (CFL GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9300H CPU @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) - 15.49 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

What it says in the title. I really didn't expect this, and I feel like it makes the debugging more unreliable. Especially because we can change the game's state while it is paused, where it should be closer to a read only snapshot of the current state.

It also calls them when the project is paused from encountering an error, so if your property has an error inside it, you will constantly print it.

### Steps to reproduce

Inspect the node with this code in the remote inspector, also place a breakpoint in `_ready`
```gdscript
extends Node

var int_var: int
var prop: String:
    get():
        int_var += 1
        prints("get prop")
        return "aaa"
    set(_v):
        prints("set prop")

func _ready() -> void:
    print("place debugger breakpoint here")
    print(int_var)
```
Ofc you shouldn't change other variables in getters, but it still calls setter when you change the property in the remote inspector. It is here just to show that the state of the paused project is being constantly changed.
